newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates see-saw to end up on OMO.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates see-saw to end up on OMO.

text.p: Pakistan's money rates fluctuated on Tuesday, but rebounded to end up after a special open market operation (OMO) by the central bank, dealers said.

"Borrowers kept bids at around 13 percent, while lenders offered overnights at 19.5 percent in early trade," a dealer said. Reasonable amounts were traded at 17 percent, but the rates slid as low as 14 percent. "Rates escalated back to 19 percent as soon as the news of the OMO cut-off hit the market."
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan accepted bids worth 6.325 billion rupees in its special OMO for the sale of Short-Term Federal Bonds at a cut-off yield of 17.40 percent.
Dealers said one- and three-month offers were quoted at 15.75 and 16.50 percent respectively.
